newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Buba's Issing calls for strict EMU stability pact.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Issing calls for strict EMU stability pact.

text.p: Bundesbank board member Otmar Issing called on Friday for the adoption of automatic sanctions when an EU state participating in the European single currency fails to keep its finances sound.

"The adoption of a 'stability pact with political bite', that means automatic sanctions if possible, can make an important contribution to building confidence", Issing told the annual meeting of the European Mortgage Federation.
Discussions are likely to heat up in the coming months on the issue of a stability pact linking EU members which adopt the Euro, the single currency due to be launched in 1999.
Under a proposal put forward by the European Commission earlier this month, countries running a budget defict higher than the three percent permitted in the Maastricht treaty may face sanctions.
Such provision is foreseen in the treaty itself, but the stability pact proposal streamlines the procedures.

Under the Commission's draft, sanctions will be applied unless an excessive deficit results from a "severe economic downturn", in particular in the case of significant negative annual real growth, or "an unusual event outside the control" of the offending country.
The Commission refused to define any such events or to quantify a severe recession.
Issing thought that a figure should be put on the negative growth concept and suggested a kind of catalogue of unusual circumstances to avoid leaving too much room for interpretation.
"I think there should be a figure," said Issing, the Bundesbank's chief economist, in reply to questions, though he declined to say what it should be.
The only example of exceptional circumstances he gave was an earthquake. -- Brussels newsroom 322 2876841
